# Ctrl + Wheel Zoom

Hold **Ctrl** (or **⌘** on macOS) and scroll the mouse wheel to zoom the whole
DeepSeek Harness Web

UI.
A small chip at the frame's bottom-right corner reports the current level and
returns to 100% in

chip at the frame's bottom-right corner reports the current level and
returns to 100% in one click.
## Features
| Gesture | Result |

| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + wheel | Zoom in/out in 10% steps, 50%–200% |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `+` / `-` | Same from

the keyboard |
| `Ctrl` / `⌘` + `0` | Reset to 100% |
| Bottom-right chip | `−` / `+` step the leve
l; clicking the percentage resets |

The level is remembered in the browser (`localStorage`) and restored on the next
page load. The chip

appears only while the level is not 100%, so the frame stays
untouched in the default state.
## Install

This is an ordinary DSH **profile bundle**: plain ESM, no build step, no runtime
dependencies. It is

published on npm as
`dsh-ctrl-zoom` and can also be
installed straight from GitHub.

## Compatibility

- Tested with DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** Web GUI (Electron 44).
- The client half needs a Chrom

ium-based Harness shell. In a non-browser Host it
is inert.
- No Node dependencies and no install sc

sed Harness shell. In a non-browser Host it
is inert.
- No Node dependencies and no install scripts.
## How it works

Zoom is CSS `zoom` on `<html>`. It scales layout, text and fixed overlay layers
together like browse

r page zoom, while the app's own scroll containers keep
working. A `transform: scale()` wrapper cann

ot scroll its oversized content, and
a font-size change would only touch text.

The wheel listener runs in the capture phase on `window` and calls
`preventDefault()`, so it sees th

e gesture before app scroll containers and the
browser's native page zoom does not apply a second, i

ndependent level. A gesture
another component has already handled (`event.defaultPrevented`, for exa

mple an
embedded editor or map with its own `Ctrl`+wheel zoom) is never stolen.

Everything is registered through `ctx.effect`: unloading the plugin removes the
chip entry, both lis
teners, the stylesheet and the applied `zoom` property.
## Privacy

The plugin makes no network requests. It reads and writes one `localStorage`
key for the zoom level
and applies a CSS `zoom` value to the document element.
